name: Noor Alabed
bio: Through community cleanups, volunteer tutoring, science communication, and sustainable engineering, Noor works hard to refine her teaching skills and remains continuously involved with climate outreach. Having grown up in Canada and the Middle East, she has seen the climate crisis manifest in various ways and believes in the power of shifting narratives to inspire collective action.

name: Renee Zhao
bio: A climate advocate and firm believer in youth-driven change, Renee specializes in Bioeconomy Sciences at UBC. As former Director of Climate Education at the Canadian Youth Climate Action Team, she has been named one of Canada's Top 25 Environmentalists Under 25 and a recipient of the National Youth Climate Activism Award.

name: Amy Doyle
bio: An environmental science student heavily involved with hands-on conservation projects, Amy believes that changing a person's mindset can be just as powerful as changing the world. She hopes to create an empowering space for young people through her ambassadorship.

name: Charlotte Pearce
bio: Passionate about science communication, Charlotte believes the natural world is absolutely beautiful and wants to do everything in her power to protect it through education — showing people what is in their own backyard and why they should strive to protect it.

name: Emmanuel Chidike Agbo
bio: An Electrical and Electronic Engineering graduate passionate about climate advocacy and sustainable waste management, Emmanuel plans to partner with the IPESS institute to bring climate education to hundreds of students at his alma mater.

name: Musa Muhammad Musa
bio: A student leader and award-winning climate action advocate, Musa focuses on climate education at the grassroots level, helping people understand how their daily actions connect to global realities and empowering communities with knowledge to co-create effective solutions.

name: Rim Azaryah
bio: Driven by continuous curiosity and a love for learning, Rim is passionate about working on meaningful initiatives that contribute to the wellbeing of society. She sees the Ambassador Programme as an opportunity to grow personally and professionally while being part of a global community working toward impactful change.

name: Sophie Lee
bio: A first-year Biologist at the University of Oxford, Sophie is motivated by the idea that effective climate action requires both strong scientific understanding and the ability to communicate meaningfully. She trained at drama school for 10 years and brings energy and storytelling into everything she does.

name: Subheya Ben Khalil
bio: A political activist and journalist from Libya, Subheya believes environmental justice is deeply connected to human rights, especially for vulnerable communities most affected by climate change. She is committed to amplifying local voices from Libya and the region through storytelling and media.

name: Tanatswa Mapfumo
bio: Driven by first-hand experience of climate change's devastating effects in the Global South, Tanatswa hopes to be a focal point for change in Zimbabwe. He founded Agrow263, a startup bringing climate journalism and education to his community.

name: Buse Korkmaz
bio: A 6th-year medical student in Istanbul and founder of a youth group, Buse became an activist after witnessing how geography becomes destiny for many people. She advocates for awareness of how vulnerable human life is to climate change and environmental inequality.

name: Chanina (Nina) Mabasa
bio: An Environmental Science graduate from UC Berkeley, Nina currently works in sustainability media. Driven by the struggles of her fellow Filipinos — one of the communities most prone to the effects of the climate crisis — she hopes to improve climate communication for local communities.
